newsitem.title: USA: US reaches 'open skies' aviation pact with Jordan.
newsitem.headline: US reaches 'open skies' aviation pact with Jordan.

text.p: The United States and Jordan have concluded an "open skies" aviation agreement to fully liberalize civil air traffic between the two countries, the State Department said on Tuesday.

Department spokesman Glyn Davies said the pact, which ends restrictions on routes and frequencies of flights by airlines of each country, was signed in Amman by the U.S. ambassador there, Wesley William Egan, and Jordanian Transport Minister Nasser al-Lawzi.
Davies said the pact was the first "open skies" accord that Washington has signed with an aviation partner in the region.
"It advances U.S. international aviation interests and further strengthens the close and friendly relations between the United States and Jordan," Davies said.
